newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Former EU official sees EMU fuelling strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Former EU official sees EMU fuelling strong dollar.

text.p: A former senior official of the European Commission predicted on Thursday that European economic and monetary union (EMU) would lead to a stronger dollar.
Bernard Connolly, former head of the Commission's monetary unit, told a news conference that weak growth in core European economies necessited a depreciation of their currencies.
"I think the approach to EMU has to be through depreciation of core European currencies," Connolly said.

Connolly, who left the Commission earlier this year after publishing a controversial book on the single currency, said the only path towards economic rejuvenation in the EU was via currency depreciation.
In turn, such an outcome would benefit the dollar.
"I think we are going to see a period of several years of upward pressure on the dollar," he added.
Regarding the prospects of the single currency being launched on schedule, Connolly said he had marked down the chances for timely implementation.
A few months ago he had estimated the probability of EMU happening at around 85 percent, but after recent events he said the odds now were about 60 percent in favour.
There was now around a 20 percent chance that France would throw in the towel.
He said the French banking system was continuing to suffer strains and the French political system was showing signs of deteriorating.
